tasks.short: Inform pilots of traffic and hazardous conditions

steps.what: Read actual traffic, weather, wind and visibility information relevant to the aircraft
inputs: actual traffic display and visual observations
actual current weather, wind and visibility reports

steps.what: Determine the relevant nearby aircraft or hazard and formulate the exact pilot-addressed information to transmit
inputs: controller-read traffic and hazard information
actual aircraft identity, position and operational context
outputs: controller-selected final pilot information and aircraft recipient

steps.what: Transmit the selected nearby-traffic or hazardous-condition information to the intended pilot
inputs: controller-selected final pilot information and aircraft recipient
outputs: actual pilot-addressed traffic or hazard information transmission

tasks.design: Retain actual traffic/weather interpretation and pilot communication with the controller using {OTHER}, the existing air-traffic displays and radio. Information retrieval, selection of exact message/recipient and radio transmission are separate; no additional display or automated transmission change is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: The useful warning depends on the aircraft's actual traffic and hazard context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing operational displays provide the information; no further supported change removes controller work.
tasks.still_hard: Freshness, relevance and correct aircraft addressing require real-time judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Choose and communicate what the particular pilot needs at that moment.

ambition.what: No automated pilot information transmission proposed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pilot traffic/hazard information requires actual source interpretation, aircraft addressing and controller communication.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means existing air-traffic surveillance/weather displays and operational radio, not a generic corporate system.

Existing surveillance/weather services produce the actual reports; no new structured feed or automatic hazard conclusion is assumed. Missing or stale information follows existing operational handling.
Retrieval is explicit and fully retained. The actual final message and aircraft recipient are chosen before its separate transmission; this is ordinary controller work, not an added approval meeting.
No separate record or report is established by this information statement. All work remains, gross/net saving are zero and no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Actual installed displays and operating procedures
research_questions: Does the actual approved system offer a native retrieval feature that changes a specific controller action?

incremental.description: No new operational system or process proposed

approvals.approved_version: controller-selected final pilot information and aircraft recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to actual source retrieval, controller judgment or pilot transmission.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor aircraft in the assigned airspace

steps.what: Monitor actual aircraft within the specific airspace using radar, computer displays and visual references as appropriate
inputs: actual radar/computer surveillance and visual references
assigned airspace and actual aircraft information
outputs: controller's actual aircraft-position and movement observations

steps.what: Interpret the observed aircraft movements, identity uncertainties and developing situations within the assigned airspace
inputs: controller's actual aircraft-position and movement observations
actual airspace context and surveillance limitations

tasks.design: Retain aircraft observation and airspace interpretation with the controller using {OTHER}, the installed surveillance displays. These displays are already today's means; no new automation or reduced observation requirement is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: The controller needs an accurate evolving picture of the actual airspace.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing surveillance supports the work but is not a new labour-saving change.
tasks.still_hard: Uncertain identity, coverage limits and changing aircraft movements require continuous judgment.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the displayed situation is incomplete or inconsistent with other observations.

ambition.what: No reduced controller monitoring duty claimed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: installed radar/computer surveillance supports aircraft monitoring but its existing runtime is not an additional controller labour saving.

assumptions: Shares are illustrative human monitoring effort, not elapsed radar/computer runtime.
OTHER means existing air-traffic surveillance. Existing surveillance services and visual observation produce the actual evidence; no new structured situation assessment is assumed.
Actual lookup/display reading is explicit. This monitoring statement establishes no separate log write, report or send; none is invented.
No change is proposed, so gross/net saving are zero and no incremental upkeep is required.
unknowns: Actual surveillance capabilities and monitoring requirements
research_questions: Does the installed approved system provide a specific unused native feature that changes human work?

incremental.description: No new monitoring system or process proposed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Existing surveillance and human situation assessment remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor, direct and sequence aircraft movements

steps.what: Monitor actual air/ground aircraft movements and read the relevant flight-strip and airport information
inputs: actual surveillance/visual aircraft movements
existing flight strips and airport operating information
outputs: controller-read movement situation and flight context

steps.what: Determine the appropriate movement sequence and exact aircraft-addressed direction or clearance
inputs: controller-read movement situation and flight context
actual operational constraints and established procedures
outputs: controller-selected final aircraft direction or clearance and recipient

steps.what: Transmit the selected movement direction or clearance to the intended aircraft
inputs: controller-selected final aircraft direction or clearance and recipient
outputs: actual transmitted movement direction or clearance

steps.what: Listen to the pilot's actual readback and monitor the resulting movement for compliance or correction needs
inputs: actual transmitted movement direction or clearance
pilot's actual readback and resulting aircraft movement
outputs: controller-checked acknowledged direction and movement response

steps.what: Update and check the actual flight-strip movement/clearance entry where the operating procedure requires it
inputs: controller-checked acknowledged direction and movement response
existing flight-strip record requirements

steps.what: Save the completed checked movement/clearance entry in the existing electronic flight strip
inputs: complete checked actual movement/clearance entry

tasks.design: Retain sequencing, directions and readback checking with the controller using {OTHER}, the existing surveillance, operational radio and electronic flight-strip systems. The actual clearance transmission and any required strip update are separate actions; existing native strip entry is retained with no new labour-saving claim.
tasks.previous_blocker: Aircraft sequencing requires actual movement context and immediate operational judgment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing displays and strips support the work; they are not a new change.
tasks.still_hard: Traffic changes and incorrect readbacks require timely controller intervention.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a safe workable sequence and verify what the pilot actually understood.

ambition.what: No automatic clearance or sequencing authority proposed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: aircraft sequencing includes actual direction transmission, readback checking and applicable flight-strip updates; existing electronic strips are already part of current work.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means existing surveillance, radio and electronic flight-strip systems.
Surveillance/flight-information services supply actual inputs; the controller creates the direction in s2; pilots supply actual readback and movement response after s3.
This scenario includes an actual required strip entry, split from communication and fully retained. No automatic completion is inferred from planned movement.
The exact aircraft-addressed direction is selected before transmission; any changed direction requires a new decision/transmission. The completed strip entry is checked before save.
No system change is proposed, so gross/net saving are zero and no new upkeep is introduced. Same-system save is negligible and earns no saving.
unknowns: Actual strip-entry requirements and native workflow
research_questions: Is there a distinct repeated record action beyond current native strips that an approved configuration could remove?

incremental.description: No new sequencing, communication or record system proposed

approvals.approved_version: controller-selected final aircraft direction or clearance and recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual monitoring, sequencing, communication and existing native strip entry remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Alert airport emergency services to emergencies or aircraft difficulties

steps.what: Assess the actual emergency or aircraft difficulty from the pilot report and current operational observations
inputs: pilot's actual difficulty/emergency report
actual aircraft position and operational observations

steps.what: Determine the required emergency-service alert and exact available aircraft, location and emergency details to communicate
inputs: controller's actual assessed emergency information
existing airport emergency contact/procedure information
outputs: controller-selected final emergency alert and service recipients

steps.what: Alert the intended airport emergency services with the selected actual emergency information
inputs: controller-selected final emergency alert and service recipients

steps.what: Receive and check the emergency services' actual acknowledgement and clarify the information if requested
inputs: actual airport emergency-service alert transmission
emergency services' actual acknowledgement and questions
outputs: actual acknowledged emergency alert and clarification

tasks.design: Retain emergency assessment and alerting with the controller using {OTHER}, the existing operational radio and emergency communication channels. The exact alert details and service recipients are determined before the distinct transmission; acknowledgement remains an actual communication task.
tasks.previous_blocker: An alert must reflect the real aircraft difficulty and available information.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing emergency channels support transmission; no additional mechanism is established that removes controller work.
tasks.still_hard: Information can be incomplete and evolve while the emergency is unfolding.
tasks.human_edge: Communicate the relevant known facts clearly without inventing missing details.

ambition.what: No automatic emergency classification or alert dispatch proposed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: actual emergency alerting includes assessment, recipient/message selection, transmission and acknowledgement using established operational channels.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured. OTHER means operational radio and airport emergency communication systems.
Pilots and existing surveillance supply actual emergency/location information; the controller selects known facts, marking unknown details rather than inferring them.
No new structured emergency packet or automatic dispatch is assumed. Message selection is actual controller work, not a separate approval ceremony.

The alert is a separate gated transmission and fully retained. This statement establishes no separate report/log; none is invented. All work remains, gross/net saving are zero and no new upkeep is required.
unknowns: Actual emergency communication mechanism and acknowledgement procedure
research_questions: Does the approved emergency system offer a specific native feature that changes a repeated controller action?

incremental.description: No new emergency communication system or process proposed

approvals.approved_version: controller-selected final emergency alert and service recipients

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No supported change to assessment, actual alert transmission or acknowledgement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

skills_to_grow: No new skills required by the unchanged design
role.ambitious_version: Controller monitoring, aircraft directions and emergency communication remain unchanged; no unsupported labour saving or decision transfer is claimed.
